text:
tera: quick design sync 1: experimenting with a compact token badge that sits at the bubbles top-right corner (small circle) showing an updating number + subtle gradient fill to indicate streaming progress. goal: keep composer height stable and avoid an extra rail. thoughts?

josh: love the compactness, but two concerns: 1) small numeric badges can fail contrast for low-vision users, 2) gradient implies progress percent but token estimator is fuzzy. might confuse users.

mika: propose variants before we pick: A) numeric badge + microcopy beneath input saying "estimating..." while streaming, B) numeric badge with tilde prefix ("~42") to signal approximate, C) progress-only ring (no number) with tooltip on hover that shows exact/approx when available.

tera: good split. i'd lean B for clarity. also want to make the stop/regenerate affordance adjacent to the composer actions (icon-only) not inside the bubble so mobile hit targets stay consistent.

a11y-bot: accessibility checklist: if badge < 14px, ensure 3:1 contrast versus background; provide an offscreen aria-label that reads e.g. "Tokens used, updating: approximately 42" and expose final label when stream completes. Use aria-live="polite" and throttle updates to 400ms. Avoid numeric-only focus targets.

remy: keyboard flow question: we currently use Esc to cancel and Cmd+Enter to send. accidental Esc cancels a draft in some browsers. suggestion: S = stop streaming (single key), R = regenerate when focus is in composer (requires explicit opt-in), keep Esc as global cancel only when composer empty. thoughts?

josh: single-key shortcuts are nice but problematic in text fields. Could we support Ctrl+S / Alt+S while composer has focus? or a dedicated small stop button that is tabbable and has an accesskey? Accesskeys are funky cross-platform.

mika: UX compromise: show the stop icon in the composer controls with a tooltip describing the keyboard mapping and expose "Hold S" vs "Tap S" behavior: tap to stop, hold to open regenerate menu. reduces accidental regen.

tera: implementation note: token estimator runs on streamed deltas which are dense. keep UI update cheap and debounce estimator calculations separately from render frames. sample debounce: ```js
let lastUpdate = 0;
function maybeUpdateTokens(n) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (now - lastUpdate > 400) { setTokenBadge(n); lastUpdate = now; }
}
```

a11y-bot: microcopy suggestion for final state: "Generation complete  final tokens: 98" and for streaming: "Approximately 45 tokens (updating)". keep labels short.

josh: copy nits 1: use "Approximately" not "Estimating"; 2: surface "final tokens" only when generation ends to avoid users misreading.

mika: prompt library conflict: floating drawer currently pops over the composer and hides the badge on small widths. propose moving prompt-library toggle to the composer toolbar overflow (right side) and making drawer push the canvas instead of overlap on narrower screens.

tera: visuals: try two color systems in the prototype: neutral numeric badge (dark text on light badge) vs accent gradient ring (accent color on transparent background). we should A/B them for clarity and contrast.

remy: test plan: small cohort (internal) with screen-reader on, keyboard-only navigation, and low-bandwidth simulation. log metrics: number of accidental regenerates, stop key collisions, and perceived latency of token badge (user-reported).

a11y-bot: add to prototype doc: https://redwood.design/proto/compact-token-badge/v1. checklist appended: aria-live cadence (400ms), offscreen text pattern, focus order, contrast tokens.

josh: next steps: add the numeric tilde variant and the progress-only ring to the prototype, wire keyboard behavior as a feature flag, and run the 5-person accessibility pass.

tera: thanks all. i'll capture the todos: 1) prototype A/B (tilde vs ring), 2) move prompt library toggle to composer overflow on narrow widths, 3) aria-live at 400ms and offscreen labels, 4) keyboard mapping experiment (S tap/hold pattern), 5) microcopy updates. tagging design/research for a quick review. :raised_hands:
